The three functions it calls - audit_contract, probe_environment and read_saved_result - are the functions of the CPU-only audit service (modal_cpu_audit_app.py) and they are named in core.r1_bounds.UNAUTHORISED_CALL_SITES, so the R1 gate refuses them at the call boundary as well. The server dispatches nothing in production: it declares gpu=None, it never touches the R1 registry, the approval key, the rate card or the production dispatch, and it reaches the audit service only through the allowlist (aegis-rlvr-cpu-audit with audit_contract, read_saved_result and probe_environment). What authorises the call is a separate maintainer approval, given out of band exactly as it is for the driver of the audit service: the MCP server requires a credential on every request (the static bearer token of the owner or an OAuth access token of its own authorization server), and the audit service checks the shared token of the Modal secret aegis-cpu-audit-auth on its own side before it does any work. A separate CPU-only application does not make an unauthorised remote workload authorised.

guard_implementation.core/r1_bounds.py: The guard itself: GuardedRemote (module-level functions), GuardedClass / GuardedClassInstance / GuardedClassMethod (the class methods, the bypass the review named) and GuardedProviderRemote (the guard installed on the provider object's own 'remote'). The guard holds no provider object: the raw objects live in the module-private registry of core.r1_bounds and the guard objects hold only an opaque token and the call-site name, so no attribute of a guard yields a raw provider callable. The guard holds no direct provider call - it delegates to the gate - so the repository has exactly one place that calls a provider: _perform_provider_call, the innermost step of the gate's dispatch, through _call_provider_entry_point. The provider entry point is not captured and not stored: it is resolved from the provider object's own class at the moment of the call, so no closure cell and no registry of the module holds an invocable provider callable. The class methods are guarded at their production boundary: the instance is moved to a subclass whose attribute resolution hands out the guard, so the method of the raw instance is guarded as well. The gate is not self-authorising: a provider dispatch additionally needs a signed approval artifact that the gate verifies itself, at dispatch time and again immediately before provider entry, against the pinned key (core/r1_approval.py) - binding not only the StepPolicy but the complete effective D26-D29 dispatch envelope (dispatch_envelope_digest) and enforcing the authoritative container_class mapping - and R1 pins no approval key, so no provider dispatch is possible in R1.
